literal: Even having given, acquiring is necessary certainly, having approached having been, unexcellent things he who does's enmity.
translation: One must certainly acquire the enmity of a person who stays close but does harmful things, even if one has to pay for it.
modern: தன்னுடனே நெருங்கியிருந்து தீமையான செயல்களைச் செய்பவனின் பகையை, ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுத்தாவது பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet advises on when enmity is actually desirable. If a person remains close as an associate but constantly does harmful or foolish things, their proximity is dangerous. Therefore, the text states that one must certainly acquire their open enmity, even if it requires giving up something valuable to achieve that separation. The word 'மாணாத' refers to actions lacking excellence or virtue, meaning harmful or treacherous deeds.
